prompt.context: Your client is an insurance company that sells home appliance insurance. They have hired you to help efficiently increase product sales.
prompt.question: What would you do to efficiently increase product sales?

clarifying_info.q: What does the insurance product cover and how is it priced?
clarifying_info.a: The client covers all appliances in the home (washer, dryer, air conditioning, refrigerator, range, etc.) for $400/year — any problems get complete repair or replacement.

clarifying_info.q: Who does the client sell to and through what channels?
clarifying_info.a: The client sells to all households in the US via two channels: a Direct Mail channel targeting 60M non-moving households, and a Sales Team channel targeting 40M moving households.

clarifying_info.q: What are the details of the Direct Mail channel?
clarifying_info.a: 50M mailers are sent each year at $0.50 per mailer, with a 0.5% sales conversion ratio.

clarifying_info.q: What are the details of the Sales Team channel?
clarifying_info.a: 80% coverage of the 40M moving households target; 5% conversion ratio; 1,000 sales team members each earning $100K annual salary.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any geographic note about coverage?
clarifying_info.a: Coverage is highly concentrated in specific regions — there is little coverage in the northeast.

framework: Analyze cost-per-customer acquisition for each sales channel
Compare channel efficiency to identify the more cost-effective approach
Identify geographic gaps and untapped opportunities
Evaluate targeting quality within each channel (e.g., indiscriminate vs. targeted mailers)
Consider adverse selection implications across channels
Recommend channel investment reallocation and geographic expansion

questions.prompt: Calculate the cost per customer acquired through the Direct Mail channel.
questions.guidance: Candidate should work through total mail cost, total new customers from conversion, then divide to find cost per customer.

math.setup: Total mail cost = mailers sent × cost per mailer; New customers = mailers sent × conversion ratio; Cost per customer = total mail cost / new customers

questions.prompt: Calculate the cost per customer acquired through the Sales Team channel.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total coverage (homes reached), new customers from conversion, total team cost, then divide to find cost per customer.

math.setup: Coverage (homes) = target market × coverage %; New customers = coverage homes × conversion ratio; Total team cost = team size × individual salary; Cost per customer = total team cost / new customers

questions.prompt: Based on the channel cost comparison, what would you recommend to efficiently increase sales?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note the Sales Team channel is meaningfully cheaper ($63 vs $100 per customer) and recommend concentrating resources on building out sales team capacity, especially in under-served regions such as the northeast.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the channel cost analysis, what additional levers could the client use to improve sales efficiency?

categories.name: Targeting & Segmentation
ideas: Send mailers only to high-potential candidates rather than indiscriminately to all non-movers
Identify demographic or behavioral profiles correlated with higher conversion

categories.name: Geographic Expansion
ideas: Build sales team capability in the northeast where coverage is currently low
Prioritize regions with high density of moving households

categories.name: Adverse Selection Management
ideas: Door-to-door sales enables selective targeting of lower-risk homes and neighborhoods rather than indiscriminate mailing
Use channel selection to screen for favorable risk profiles

categories.name: Channel Mix Optimization
ideas: Shift budget from Direct Mail toward Sales Team given lower cost per customer
Evaluate whether a smaller, more targeted mailer volume could maintain volume while cutting cost

recommendation: Shift investment toward the Sales Team channel, which acquires customers at ~$63 vs. ~$100 for Direct Mail
Prioritize building sales team presence in the northeast to close the geographic coverage gap
risks: Sales team scaling takes time and hiring/training costs may temporarily raise cost per customer
Reducing mailer volume risks losing reach in markets where the sales team has no presence
next_steps: Quantify the revenue per customer (from the $400/year premium) against acquisition cost to confirm full economics
Model the incremental cost of northeast sales team expansion vs. expected new customers
Pilot targeted mailers to high-propensity segments to test whether conversion rates improve materially
